findings.title: Organization slug spread condition is inverted, so the slug is now stored only when team billing is enabled
findings.description: The original line was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which includes `slug` when billing is disabled. The replacement `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses that, so `slug` is dropped in the non-billing case and written only when billing is on. The `requestedSlug` line on the next changed line keeps the original sense, so the two fields now diverge.

findings.title: Non-calendar `credentialId` is replaced with `undefined` in the video/other-app branch
findings.description: The original expression was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so non-calendar results keep `result.credentialId`. The new expression is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Non-calendar results (video and other apps) now lose their `credentialId`, which breaks later lookups of those references. The calendar branch was the only part that should have changed.

findings.title: Google `updateEvent` fallback calendar lookup compares against the falsy `externalCalendarId` and can never match
findings.description: In the `: ` branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : ...`, `externalCalendarId` is already known to be falsy. The new `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` therefore compares each `externalId` against a falsy value and returns `undefined` for any real calendar. The previous code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The fallback calendar is now always `undefined`, so updates go to the wrong calendar or fail. The lookup should use the destination's own identity, not `externalCalendarId`.

findings.title: Google `deleteEvent` fallback has the same never-matching `find` on the falsy `externalCalendarId`
findings.description: The `calendarId` ternary repeats the defect from `updateEvent`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` cannot select a real calendar, so `calendarId` is `undefined` and the delete targets nothing useful. The original used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

findings.title: Unguarded `.integration` access on a possibly undefined first destination calendar throws a TypeError
findings.description: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. Any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar will throw here, where the original used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. The access should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.
